findings.title: Interpolating before querySupportsSplitting can defeat the $__range split guard
findings.body: runSplitQuery() now replaces template variables in query.expr at line 299 and only afterwards, at line 300, partitions queries with querySupportsSplitting(). That helper is documented at lines 282-288 to keep queries containing $__range, $__range_s or $__range_ms out of splitting so the backend can interpolate the range against the unsplit time range. If applyTemplateVariables() substitutes those range variables (as it does other variables such as $__auto/$step in the new test), the marker is gone before the check, the query is classified as splittable, and every time chunk is sent with the range value frozen from the original panel range, producing incorrect rate/range results instead of the intended single unsplit request. The splittability check needs to be done on the pre-interpolation expression or range variables must be provably preserved and covered by a test.

findings.title: Shard-split queries are interpolated twice, once per shard group
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery() interpolates every target with datasource.applyTemplateVariables() at line 52, adds the __stream_shard__ selector, and then delegates each shard group to runSplitQuery() (line 163), which after this change interpolates the same targets again at querySplitting.ts:299. The updated test codifies this: a single target now triggers applyTemplateVariables 5 times (1 initial + 1 per shard sub-request). Template interpolation with scopedVars and ad-hoc filters (request.filters is passed in both places) is not a guaranteed idempotent operation: variable values containing '$', $__auto/step derivation, and ad-hoc filter injection into the stream selector can be applied a second time to an already interpolated/shard-augmented expression, and the redundant work scales with the number of shard groups. runSplitQuery needs a way for the shard path to skip re-interpolation, or the shard path should not pre-interpolate beyond what shard grouping requires.

findings.title: Empty-expression filtering now happens before interpolation in shard splitting
findings.body: The filters at lines 50-51 run before the interpolation map at line 52, whereas the previous code interpolated first and then dropped queries with no expr. A target whose expr is only a template variable (e.g. expr: '$q') that expands to an empty string now passes the filter, is interpolated to '', and continues into groupTargetsByQueryType()/getSelectorForShardValues() and on to execution as an empty LogQL query instead of being ignored, causing shard-label fetching and/or a Loki parse error for a query that should have been dropped. The expr emptiness check should also (or instead) be applied to the interpolated result; the same filter-before-map pattern was introduced in runSplitQuery at querySplitting.ts:296-299.
